> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5a5bbe05cdc2b19aacce1cbd75c0102fe2dadb0` — the merge of head `5ec0b745fd6c34ec295b1d97bfb25399366e69c4` into base `b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5a5bbe05cdc2b19aacce1cbd75c0102fe2dadb0 && git checkout c5a5bbe05cdc2b19aacce1cbd75c0102fe2dadb0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a 5ec0b745fd6c34ec295b1d97bfb25399366e69c4 && git checkout -B drift-repro b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a && git merge --no-ff 5ec0b745fd6c34ec295b1d97bfb25399366e69c4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25652 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T20:16Z · head `5ec0b745fd` · report `6388001086` and addendum `6388798472` (on #25652; cloud session `session_01AwcSGXmnoviawmFu9pGgNZ`) · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and the path limb hits (`packages/spec/src/system/**`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25652`. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` lines are line-initial in the body and the changeset (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/lint`, all `minor`). `Ruling-ref` points to triage's first grade `6385078248`: a protocol addition under the standing order, not a decision card. 24 files, +734/−23. `check-governed-merges --pr 25701`: NOT governed, 0 of 24 paths. No `content/docs/releases/**`.
2. **The grade, measured on the diff.** `appTranslationDataShape` gains `positions` and `permissions`, each a `strictObject` closed at `label` / `description` and keyed by the item's `name`. The bundle entry, the registered `translation` item and the platform bundle share that shape, so all three accept them. The `aliases` only steer the refusal's "did you mean"; the key is still refused. The changeset now says exactly that.
   - Translators: `translatePosition` / `translatePermissionSet` are registered in `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS`. `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` derives from that table, so `/meta/position` and `/meta/permission` are localized on both transports.
   - CLI: `walkSecurityCatalog` uses `pushOptional`, and `i18n/missing-position` / `i18n/missing-permission` each get their own bucket.
   - Lint (patch round 1): `translation-target-unknown` resolves `positions.NAME` against `positions[]` and `permissions.NAME` against `permissions[]`, sibling packages included via `artifactProvidedRecords`, with the audience anchors folded in. An unknown name is an `error`, the same verdict as the picklist list face.
3. **Changeset, checked line by line.** The strictness wording matches the `strictObject`. "Served in the request's locale" matches the translator registration. The lint bullet matches the new leg and its anchor fold. "A key the bundle does not carry keeps the authored string" matches the translators' miss branch, pinned in `i18n-security-catalog.test.ts`.
4. **Gates.** `ci-failure --pr 25701` GREEN: 42 check-runs on `5ec0b745fd`, all completed, none failed. Local, per the report and addendum:
   - 129/129 derived exit 0 at both `f444163b7` and `5ec0b745f`; `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
   - spec 720 / 21786 and `test:repo` 79 / 1269; cli 329 / 4821; rest 320 / 6406 and `test:repo` 5 / 280; runtime 441 / 7080 and `test:repo` 3 / 908; platform-objects 95 / 1352; metadata-protocol 263 / 21475; lint 161 / 7274 on the final head.
   - Three ablations, each restored blob-identical: the position translator (2 of 10 red), the CLI walk (5 of 5 red), the lint leg (2 of 5 red). The reverse type check (TS2353) passed.
5. **Open questions.**
   - (1) Keep the server translators past the claim's scope line, **A**. Declaring the groups without a reader would ship a key that parses and translates nothing, the declared-not-enforced shape Prime Directive #10 forbids. The datasets precedent seeds the liveness row `live` with its reader. The console pickers already read these two `/meta` lists. The claim's file surface is amended in `#25652` to match.
   - (2) An objectui card for the remaining render sites, **A**. The seat files it at this PR's merge, scoped to wherever objectui shows a position or permission-set label from a payload other than `/meta/position` / `/meta/permission` (approval steps, sharing and assignment UIs), measured against the pin then current.
6. **Deviations and boundaries.**
   - Continuing past "stop on breach" is accepted for the reason in (1). The dev named it in the report rather than doing it silently.
   - `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 3.
   - Boundary, for the contract review: platform permission sets get no fold in the new lint leg, the same posture as the picklist leg. A stack bundle that translates a platform-declared permission set by name is reported as an orphan `error`. Measured producers: HotCRM `8a14b56` has no `positions` / `permissions` translation group, and the examples pass the gate. No carrier.
   - The stale `RECORDED_DECLARED` / `RECORDED_WALKED` sample in `scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs` is noted, no carrier. Its header says it is a sample, not a source of truth.
   - The PR body is edited by the seat in this stroke, as the dev proposed.
7. **Landing.** Not governed, 757 changed lines. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
